messages:
Anya: heads-up: CI red on main for the serving runtime tests, flakey failure in `serve/tests/retry_backoff_test.py::test_concurrent_retries` 
Anya: failing intermittently, I hit it twice in a row locally and once in CI. logs attached below. can someone trigger a rerun / bisect? @Sam? :eyes:
ci-bot: Build 9842 failed on linux-x86-64 (tests failed) — https://ci.internal.redwood/9842 | rerun: click to retrigger
Anya: failing trace snippet:
```
E       AssertionError: expected 3 retries, got 2
serve/runtime/retries.py:142: AssertionError
Thread-7: sleep(0.01) returned early
Thread-12: backoff scheduled at 0.032s
```
Anya: it's odd because timestamps/ordering look nondet — sometimes we get 3 retries recorded, sometimes 2. can't reproduce in docker with `pytest -k retry` unless run in parallel
Sam: ack, will rerun CI now
Sam: rerun triggered: https://ci.internal.redwood/9842/retry (started) :rocket:
Prateek: quick thought — we've seen races where the retry counter is incremented in a non-atomic path when exceptions are swallowed by the executor. diff that changed the executor last month touched that area.
Jen: do we have flaky history on that test? heatmap?
Anya: query says 7 failures in the past 30 days, mostly on linux-x86-64 and sometimes macos. windows no failures.
Prateek: sounds like a timing ordering issue. two suggestions: (1) add deterministic seed for the scheduler in the test harness, (2) try a bisect between commits touching `runtime/executor.*`
Sam: CI rerun finished: Build 9842 retry -> passed (flaky) :tada:
Anya: ok passed this time. still want to bisect though to prevent regression creeping back in
Prateek: I'm happy to bisect. can someone point me to a minimal repro command?
Anya: local repro that sometimes triggers:
```
# run the serving runtime tests with parallel workers
export RW_SCHEDULER_JITTER=1
pytest serve/tests/retry_backoff_test.py::test_concurrent_retries -n auto -q
```
Note: the `RW_SCHEDULER_JITTER=1` env toggles extra jitter in CI which increases flakiness, so it's useful to reproduce timing edge cases.
Prateek: thanks. I'll start bisecting between `main~50` and `main~1` to narrow down. will post progress here.
Sam: ping me if you need CI artifacts; I can upload core dumps/log bundles.
Jen: also add annotated TODO to test: mark flaky and add short info on how to reproduce until we fix (so other devs know).
Anya: agree — I'll open a small PR to annotate the test and add the env-based repro snippet to its docstring.
Prateek: first bisect run starting now. if I find a suspect commit I'll request a targeted rerun.
ci-bot: Bisect job 345 started by Prateek on commit range main~50..main~1
Prateek: early signal: suspect commit touching `runtime/executor.py` at main~27 increases parallel completion ordering by removing a small `sleep(0.001)` that used to yield. trying a narrower range.
Anya: that matches my hunch. that sleep used to be a hack but maybe held a hidden ordering guarantee.
Sam: if bisect confirms, fix options: reintroduce a controlled yield, or make the retry counter update atomic under lock, or change test to not rely on ordering.
Jen: prefer fixing code (atomic counter) + keep test more robust. tests depending on timing are brittle.
Prateek: noted. will try reverting that change as a patch to validate.
Anya: thanks all. please add short notes on any findings. I'll open the annotated test PR now.
Sam: thanks — keep us posted :thumbsup:
Prateek: bisect update: narrowed to main~30..main~24, running focused bisect jobs. next update in ~20m.
Anya: tracked in issue #INF-412 (flaky: concurrent retries test) — adding links to CI runs and local repro.
Jen: awesome. once we have a fix we should roll a canary to dedicated and run the heavy concurrency e2e for 24h.
ci-bot: Bisect job 345 updated: step 6/12 passed
Prateek: step 9/12 failed — suspect commit is main~27 (author: kyle). I'll open a draft revert PR to validate behavior.
Anya: if revert fixes, we can evaluate proper fix. thanks everyone.
